description:
A SINGLE UNINTERRUPTED PANORAMIC PAINTING of one continuous antique dealer's cabinet interior, rendered as ONE flowing seamless mural with absolutely NO vertical lines dividing the image, NO triptych frames, NO panels, NO image seams, NO black borders between any parts — strictly forbidden to split the image into thirds or sections; the result must read as a single oil-painted scroll-like view of the same room.

IMPORTANT compositional constraint: this panorama will be viewed on a smartphone that swipes horizontally, snapping to one of three viewing windows. Each viewing window shows roughly a third of the image (0–33%, 33–66%, 66–100% of the width). For this reason, NO key element (no door, no window, no piece of furniture, no major architectural feature) may straddle the vertical positions at 33% or 66% of the image. The areas around 33% and 66% must contain ONLY plain continuous wallpaper / empty wall surface — they are the 'breathing zones' where one viewing window transitions to the next.

Architecture (described continuously across the width): the viewer looks into a cozy three-walled interior. At the far LEFT (roughly 0–18%), a LEFT SIDE WALL angles forward toward the viewer. From 18% to 82% we see the FLAT BACK WALL straight on. From 82% to the right edge, a RIGHT SIDE WALL angles forward toward the viewer. The walls meet at TWO interior corners (around 18% and 82%) — visible only as a soft change of wall plane and gentle painted shading at the join, never as a hard line. ONE continuous wooden parquet floor runs unbroken across the bottom. ONE continuous ceiling moulding runs unbroken across the top. Vintage damask wallpaper covers the entire continuous wall surface.

Feature details by horizontal position (0% = left edge, 100% = right edge):

• 0–22% — STRONG FOREGROUND ANCHOR: a substantial MAHOGANY WRITING DESK juts forward from the LEFT-BOTTOM CORNER of the image into the viewer's space, the front edge cropping out of frame on the left. We see the near front corner of the desk and its full top surface from a slight top-down 3/4 angle, with the desk oriented so that its long side runs from the left-foreground back-right toward the back wall — a person sitting at this desk would FACE the back-wall window (see below). On the desk surface: a few scattered sheets of parchment, a brass inkwell with a quill pen, a small green-shade Art Déco desk lamp lit warmly, a leather-cornered blotter pad. Leave generous bare areas on the desk top so that small additional objects (a rolled newspaper, a notebook) can be composited on later.
• 0–18% — LEFT SIDE WALL behind the desk: a TALL BUILT-IN BOOKSHELF running floor-to-ceiling, packed with old leather-bound books and a brass bookshelf rail. The bookshelf is on the angled side wall, partly behind the desk.
• 22–30% — on the BACK WALL: a tall WOODEN-FRAMED WINDOW set at normal ground-floor height (NOT high under the ceiling — sill around mid-wall, around the desk surface height), with multiple panes divided by wooden mullions. The interior of the panes shows a PAINTED VIEW of a Parisian street at GROUND-FLOOR level, NOT a view of rooftops or sky alone: we see across the cobbled street to the opposite side, where a classic Haussmannian building facade with stone balustrades and tall french windows runs along the street; chestnut tree trunks and lower foliage along the sidewalk; a wrought-iron gas streetlamp; perhaps the suggestion of a passer-by silhouette. Soft impressionistic brushstrokes, warm pastel midday daylight. Same Art Déco rendering as the rest of the image (sepia ink + soft wash). This window is the one the desk faces.
• 33% area — only plain continuous damask wallpaper (BREATHING ZONE for the swipe boundary between the desk view and the door view). No door frame, no window, no furniture here.
• 42–58% — on the BACK WALL: a heavy wooden FRONT DOOR with a polished brass letterbox slot at mid-height, set flush into the back wall, no protruding frame breaking the wall plane. EXTREMELY IMPORTANT: the door's vertical centerline MUST be at EXACTLY the 50% horizontal position of the entire panorama — perfectly centered to the left/right edges of the image. The door occupies horizontal 42–58% (8% padding on each side from its centerline). A thin Persian runner on the parquet floor in front of the door leads up to it, also centered. The composition around the door must be symmetric.
• ~50% on the CEILING: an ART DÉCO BRASS PENDANT CEILING LAMP (plafonnier) hangs down from the center of the ceiling above the door — a multi-tiered chandelier with frosted glass tulip shades casting a warm pool of light down toward the door. The lamp's chain stays well above the door, never crossing into the floor area.
• 66% area — only plain continuous damask wallpaper (BREATHING ZONE for the swipe boundary between the door view and the fireplace view). No window, no fireplace edge, no furniture here.
• 70–78% — on the BACK WALL: a second tall WOODEN-FRAMED WINDOW set at the SAME ground-floor height as the left window (sill around mid-wall), symmetrical to the one at 22–30%. The interior of the panes shows the PAINTED VIEW continuing further down the same Parisian street at GROUND-FLOOR level: more of the opposite Haussmannian building facade with a corner café terrace and round bistro tables on the sidewalk, more chestnut trunks, a second wrought-iron gas streetlamp. Same warm pastel midday daylight, same impressionistic Art Déco rendering style. NO rooftops, NO sky-only view — keep the street level visible.
• 82–100% — RIGHT SIDE WALL with a STONE FIREPLACE (small warm fire burning in the hearth, carved stone mantelpiece with a few decorative trinkets, chimney column rising to the ceiling). The fireplace front faces the viewer at 3/4 angle. A large Persian rug on the parquet floor in the foreground (78–100%), a small wooden side table, and a clear empty floor space (no objects) reserved for an armchair that will be composited later.

Lighting: soft warm directional light from the upper-left, consistent across the whole panorama (back-wall windows + desk lamp + pendant lamp + fireplace all reinforce a cozy lit interior). Cohesive Art Déco rendering: cream parchment paper texture, sepia ink line-art, soft forest green wash, brass and warm wood tones, subtle paper grain. No people, no text, no captions, no signatures, no watermark.

CRITICAL FINAL CONSTRAINTS — (a) Both back-wall windows show a painted view of the SAME Parisian street at GROUND-FLOOR level (across the street: Haussmannian facades, chestnut trees, sidewalk, gas lamps). Absolutely NO rooftops, NO sky-only view, NO view from above — we are at street level. No transparent areas anywhere in the image — the PNG is fully opaque. (b) Absolutely no vertical seams, no black bars, no panel borders anywhere in the image. (c) NOTHING (no furniture, no door, no window, no architectural feature) crosses the vertical position at 33% or 66% of the image — those zones contain only continuous damask wallpaper. (d) The front door is PERFECTLY CENTERED at the 50% horizontal position of the image, with the rest of the composition symmetric around that centerline.

A heavy wooden front door, closed, with a polished brass letterbox slot at mid-height. The door is intended to be composited on top of the CENTER zone of the reference image (the entrance wall), at the exact same position, perspective and scale as the door already shown in the reference. Match the reference's eye-level perspective, the soft warm light from upper-left, the rendering style (Art Déco line-art + sepia/forest green wash on cream parchment), and the door's apparent height in the reference. Isolated subject only — door panel, frame and letterbox visible — on transparent background, nothing else.

A vintage tufted Chesterfield armchair in deep emerald-green velvet, three-quarter front view facing slightly toward the viewer. The armchair is intended to be placed on the Persian rug in the RIGHT zone (reading nook) of the reference image, in the empty floor space between the side table and the fireplace. Match the reference's eye-level perspective, scale (the armchair should fit naturally on the rug without overlapping the fireplace), and lighting (soft warm light from upper-left). Use the same Art Déco line-art + sepia/forest green wash style on cream parchment. Isolated subject on transparent background — armchair only, no rug, no nook elements.

A rolled-up vintage newspaper tied with a string, lying flat on a desk surface. The newspaper is intended to be placed on the mahogany writing desk in the LEFT zone of the reference image, viewed from the same slight top-down angle the desk surface has. Match the reference's perspective, scale (the rolled newspaper should look like a regular ~40cm log on the desk), lighting from upper-left, and the same Art Déco line-art + sepia/forest green wash style. Isolated subject on transparent background — newspaper only, no desk.

A small leather-bound notebook, closed, brown cover with gilded edges, lying flat next to the rolled newspaper on the same writing desk. The notebook is intended to be placed on the mahogany writing desk in the LEFT zone of the reference image. Match the reference's perspective (same slight top-down angle as the desk), scale (notebook ~A6 size on the desk), lighting from upper-left, and the same Art Déco rendering style. Isolated subject on transparent background — notebook only, no desk.

ONLY the vintage gramophone itself: a polished wooden box (the soundbox/mechanism, ~30cm wide) with a polished brass tulip horn pointing to the upper-left. ABSOLUTELY NO furniture, NO pedestal, NO side table, NO support of any kind under the gramophone — the wooden box appears to rest flat on an invisible surface, ready to be composited on top of the small wooden side table that already exists in the reference image. Three-quarter front view, eye-level perspective matching the reference, warm soft light from upper-left, same Art Déco line-art + sepia/forest green wash style on cream parchment. Isolated subject on transparent background — wooden gramophone box + brass horn ONLY, nothing else.

A single closed white envelope as if dropped on the floor, slightly rotated, soft shadow underneath. Intended to be placed on the floor right in front of the door in the CENTER zone of the reference image. Match the reference's perspective on the floor (slight top-down) and lighting from upper-left. Same Art Déco rendering style. Isolated subject on transparent background — envelope only.

A tall vintage wooden coat rack (porte-manteau sur pied) standing upright, ~1.8m tall, with a polished brass crown of curved hooks at the top, slender turned-wood pole, weighted base ring. A felt top hat hangs on one hook; a long woolen scarf draped on another; an ebony cane with brass tip leans against the base. Three-quarter front view, eye-level perspective matching the reference, warm soft light from upper-left, same Art Déco line-art + sepia/forest green wash style on cream parchment. Intended to be placed on the parquet floor immediately to the right of the front door in the CENTER zone of the reference. Isolated subject on transparent background — coat rack and its accessories only, no wall, no floor.

OUTPAINTING TASK — the reference image is the final approved WIDE illustration of an old Parisian street with an antique dealer's house at its center (21:9 panorama). Produce a TALLER 3:2 version of the SAME scene: the ENTIRE reference image sits across the FULL WIDTH at the VERTICAL CENTER, reproduced AS FAITHFULLY AS POSSIBLE (same buildings, same house with its garage and four dormers, same street furniture, same style, same light — change NOTHING inside the original frame), and the scene EXTENDS SEAMLESSLY ABOVE and BELOW:

• TOP EXTENSION: the buildings continue upward naturally — the antique dealer's zinc mansard ridge finishes against the sky, the taller Haussmannian neighbors gain their missing upper floors and zinc roofs with chimney pots, the chestnut tree canopy at the top corners gains more foliage and branches, and above it all a soft warm late-afternoon Parisian SKY (cream-peach wash, a few thin clouds, distant rooftops and chimneys of the next street barely suggested). The wisp of smoke from the dealer's chimney rises higher into the sky.

• BOTTOM EXTENSION: the foreground COBBLED ROADWAY continues toward the viewer with the same perspective (larger worn cobblestones, subtle sheen, a few fallen chestnut leaves, faint old cart-wheel ruts) — plain roadway, NO new objects, NO vehicles, NO people; the sidewalk and its curb continue along their existing line.

The perspective, vanishing point, light direction (warm, from upper-left), palette and the Art Déco sepia ink + watercolor style on cream parchment ALL continue perfectly seamlessly — no visible seam, no change of grain between the original band and the extensions. No people, no animals except the existing rooftop cat, absolutely NO readable text anywhere, no captions, no signature, no watermark. Fully opaque image.

TILEABLE STREET SEGMENT — TWO reference images. IMAGE 1 (wide scene) is the right end of an old Parisian street: use it ONLY to calibrate style, scale, palette, light, sky band height, sidewalk/curb height and cobblestone band — do NOT reproduce its buildings. IMAGE 2 is a NARROW VERTICAL SLICE (the left edge of image 1): the new image must START and END with this exact slice — reproduce it at IDENTICAL SCALE at the FAR LEFT EDGE and again at the FAR RIGHT EDGE of the new image (full height, its tree trunk, pale facade with green shutters, small brown door, cobble rows and sky band continuing without break at both borders). Between these two edge replicas, EXACTLY ONCE each, the NEW content.

NEW CONTENT (center of the image): TWO small charming Parisian shopfronts side by side in strict FLAT FRONTAL ELEVATION (facade planes parallel to the picture plane — NO street corner, NO side street, NO vanishing-point perspective anywhere): on the left a FLOWER SHOP with soft sage-green woodwork, buckets of painted flowers (peonies, sunflowers, lavender) arranged on wooden steps spilling onto the sidewalk, hanging baskets under the fascia, NO text on its sign (just a painted rose emblem); on the right a small BOOKSHOP with deep oxblood woodwork, a warmly lit window stacked with old leather-bound books, a wooden crate of second-hand books on a small table outside, NO text on its sign (just a painted open-book emblem); between and around them quieter Haussmannian facades with shutters, wrought-iron balconets, geranium window boxes, a wrought-iron streetlamp, a couple of bollards, strings of small triangular bunting flags (faded cream and brick-red, NO text) hung across between two facades high above the street.

CONTINUITY RULES: ONE continuous flat street elevation from edge to edge; the sidewalk curb and the cobbled roadway bands run at EXACTLY the same heights as in image 2 across the whole width; the sky band keeps the same height, warm cream-peach wash, thin clouds; rooflines vary (zinc mansards, chimney pots) but stay in the same band; occasional chestnut foliage from the top edge. Warm light from upper-left. Art Déco style: sepia ink line-art, watercolor washes, cream parchment texture, subtle grain — identical to image 1.

STRICT: NO people, NO animals, NO vehicles; NO readable text AT ALL (the shop signs carry only painted emblems); no captions, no signature, no watermark; the slice replicas at both edges must be faithful enough that two copies of this image placed side by side would tile seamlessly. Fully opaque image.

A SINGLE UNINTERRUPTED PANORAMIC PAINTING of one continuous second-hand curiosity shop interior, rendered as ONE flowing seamless mural with absolutely NO vertical lines dividing the image, NO triptych frames, NO panels, NO image seams, NO black borders between any parts — strictly forbidden to split the image into thirds or sections; the result must read as a single painted scroll-like view of the same room.

MATCH THE REFERENCE IMAGE EXACTLY in rendering style, camera height, perspective and depth: single vanishing point at the horizontal centre, horizon line at about 57% of the image height, the room read as a three-walled box — a LEFT SIDE WALL angling forward from 0 to 18%, a FLAT BACK WALL seen straight on from 18% to 82%, a RIGHT SIDE WALL angling forward from 82% to the right edge. ONE continuous wooden floor runs unbroken across the bottom, ONE continuous ceiling moulding runs unbroken across the top. Same sepia ink line-art, soft watercolour wash, cream parchment paper texture, brass and warm wood tones, subtle paper grain.

IMPORTANT compositional constraint: this panorama is viewed on a smartphone that swipes horizontally, snapping to three viewing windows (0-33%, 33-66%, 66-100%). NO key element may straddle the vertical positions at 33% or 66%. Those two areas must contain ONLY plain continuous wall surface — they are the breathing zones between viewing windows.

Feature details by horizontal position (0% = left edge, 100% = right edge):

• 0-18% — LEFT SIDE WALL, the retro video-game and curiosities corner: floor-to-ceiling wooden shelving, WELL ORDERED rather than heaped — each shelf a tidy row, objects standing upright, boxes stacked squarely, like a collector's display and not a dumping ground. What stands on it is a mix of retro gaming and genuine flea-market finds: old game consoles and stacked cartridges, coiled controllers, small painted figurines, but ALSO stacks of vinyl records in their sleeves, a boxy bakelite radio, an old rotary telephone, a film camera, a pair of binoculars, a stack of hardback books, a tin biscuit box, a wind-up alarm clock. Colours dusty but legible; every object clearly readable as itself.
• 0-14% — FOREGROUND ANCHOR: a wooden crate and a stack of boxed games juts forward from the LEFT-BOTTOM CORNER into the viewer's space, cropping out of frame on the left.
• 19-32% — THE RESERVED GAP, the single most important compositional constraint of this painting. Across this whole vertical strip, from the FLOOR all the way UP to the ceiling moulding, there is NOTHING AT ALL: no shelving, no cabinet, no bookcase, no crate, no chair, no object, no picture, no shadow, no stain, no marking. Bare wall above, bare floor below, and nothing standing on that floor. The left wall's shelving MUST STOP before 19% and must not resume; the counter zone begins later. This strip must read as a conspicuously empty patch of shop — a gap a visitor would notice. An arcade cabinet will be composited into it later, and anything drawn here would collide with it.
• 33% area — plain continuous wall only (BREATHING ZONE). No furniture, no shelf edge, no object.
• 38-62% — THE COUNTER: a massive warm mahogany shop counter seen straight on, frontal, carved with simple Art Déco panels. Its top is a PLAIN SOLID WOOD SURFACE — absolutely NO glass display case, NO vitrine, NO glass of any kind. The counter top is bare EXCEPT for one object: an ORNATE ANTIQUE BRASS CASH REGISTER standing at the RIGHT END of the counter (around 57-62% of the image width), with round keys, a scrolled brass body and a small price flag on top, catching a warm highlight. The rest of the counter top — its whole left and centre — stays completely clear and empty.
• 38-62% — on the BACK WALL behind the counter: EXACTLY THREE PLAIN WOODEN SHELF BOARDS, mounted FLAT AGAINST THE FRONTAL BACK WALL (not angled, not in perspective), one above the other, evenly spaced, all three the same length, each carried by simple wooden or iron brackets. They are open planks: absolutely NO vertical dividers, NO compartments, NO side panels, NO back panel, NO cabinet or box around them — three bare boards on a bare wall, nothing more. All three are COMPLETELY EMPTY, with nothing standing on them whatsoever. Merchandise will be composited on top of them later, so their top surfaces must be clearly visible and squarely facing the viewer.
• VERTICAL PLACEMENT, measured from the TOP of the image (0% = top edge, 100% = bottom edge). These bands are mandatory and must not overlap:
  – 5% to 22%: the NEON TUBE (described below), and nothing else.
  – 22% to 26%: EMPTY WALL. A clearly visible gap of bare wall between the neon and the topmost shelf board.
  – 26% to 54%: the THREE SHELF BOARDS — the top board at 26%, the middle at 40%, the lowest at 54%. EXACTLY THREE, never four.
  – The vertical gap between two consecutive boards is therefore 14% of the image height, and that generous spacing is DELIBERATE: objects will be composited standing on each board, and they need headroom. Do not draw the boards closer together, and do not add a fourth.
  – 54% to 68%: EMPTY WALL again — the reserved band where a shopkeeper's chest and head will appear. Nothing may be drawn here.
  – 68%: the COUNTER TOP.
  The neon and the shelf boards must NEVER touch, overlap or cross. The three boards must be unobstructed from end to end — nothing hangs in front of any of them, and the cash register must not reach up to the lowest board.
• 44-56% — the floor between the counter and the back wall: RESERVED EMPTY SPACE, a clear standing area about one person wide, bare floor, nothing on it — a shopkeeper figure will be composited standing here later. Keep the floor line crisp and unobstructed.
• THE NEON TUBE — the shop's ONLY light fixture, and the single element allowed to span the whole image. ONE CONTINUOUS glass neon tube runs the entire width of the painting just below the ceiling, entering at the LEFT edge (0%) and leaving at the RIGHT edge (100%), unbroken from end to end. It SNAKES: it undulates gently up and down between 5% and 22% of the image height, a slow serpentine curve with three or four soft bends, suspended a little away from the ceiling on thin brackets. Its light CHANGES COLOUR ALONG ITS LENGTH: cold electric blue where it enters on the left, shifting through pale green-white, then honey, and finally a warm amber where it leaves on the right. The glow spills onto whatever is below it, so the left of the shop reads cool and the right reads warm, with the counter in the middle bathed in the honey-coloured stretch — the counter must still be the most inviting, best-lit spot in the room. There is NO pendant lamp, NO chandelier, NO ceiling rose: the ceiling is otherwise bare.
• 66% area — plain continuous wall only (BREATHING ZONE). No furniture, no object.
• 68-82% — the antiques corner. It is FULL but TIDY: the shop's overflow, arranged the way a dealer actually arranges stock — trunks stacked squarely one on another, picture frames leaning in an even row against the wall, carpets rolled and stood upright side by side in a corner, crockery grouped on a low chest, small objects lined up rather than scattered. Nothing lies fallen or spilled on the floor. What it contains are the things one genuinely finds at a French brocante: a grandfather clock, a pair of steamer trunks, oil lamps, a stack of picture frames, a porcelain tea service, a birdcage, rolled carpets, a treadle sewing machine, a typewriter, a copper coffee grinder, a gilt-framed mirror, a crate of vinyl records, a wooden crucifix, a folded pile of old lace and linens. DESATURATED and dusty — this area must not attract the eye, but every object must read clearly as what it is.
• 72-80% — a plain WOODEN TABLE standing in the middle of this corner, its top completely BARE and clearly readable, no objects on it at all. Reserved for later use.
• 82-100% — RIGHT SIDE WALL angling forward, with the SHOP'S FRONT DOOR set into it, seen at a three-quarter angle: a wooden door with a large frosted glass pane, a small brass bell above it, warm daylight streaming in through the glass and spilling onto the floor. This daylight is the second bright accent of the painting.

Colour: the painting is gently muted and dusty, but NOT washed out and NEVER grey — it must feel like a warm, lived-in shop, not a pencil study. Soft sage-green walls, honey and mahogany woods, brass that glows, and scattered low-saturation accents among the clutter: faded red and teal on the boxed games, ochre and dusty blue on the antiques, a worn carpet with colour left in it. The two light sources — the counter's pendant lamp and the daylight at the door — are the warmest, brightest points. Keep every colour a step below full saturation, so that the bright objects composited on top later still stand out.

Lighting: soft warm directional light from the upper-left, consistent across the whole panorama. NO people anywhere. ABSOLUTELY NO LETTERING OF ANY KIND: no text, no words, no captions, no labels, no shop signs, no titles on book spines or record sleeves or boxes, no signatures, no watermark. Every sign, plaque, label and spine must be blank or carry only an abstract decorative pattern — a single written word anywhere makes the painting unusable. No transparent areas — the image is fully opaque.

CRITICAL FINAL CONSTRAINTS — (a) Behind the counter there are EXACTLY THREE bare wooden shelf BOARDS — open planks with no dividers, no compartments and no cabinet around them — hung at mid-wall height with a chest-high band of bare wall between the lowest board and the counter, never overlapped by the neon; the counter top carries NO glass case and nothing but the brass cash register at its right end. (b) The arcade gap (19-32%) is empty from floor to ceiling — no shelving, no furniture, no object, no shadow; the shopkeeper spot (44-56%) and the table top (72-80%) are EMPTY and unobstructed too. If the left wall's shelving runs past 19%, the painting is wrong. (c) Nothing crosses the vertical positions at 33% or 66% — with THREE deliberate exceptions, which must run unbroken across the whole width: the floor, the ceiling moulding, and the neon tube. In particular THE COUNTER IS STRICTLY CONTAINED BETWEEN 38% AND 62% OF THE WIDTH: its LEFT edge must start after 38% and never reach 33%, and its right edge, and the cash register standing on it, must stop well before 66%, leaving a clear strip of bare floor and wall between the counter's right edge and the antiques corner. (d) No vertical seams, no panel borders, no black bars anywhere.
